subject: Compute surge and reserved-capacity delta — immediate mitigation plan
messages:
From: James Liu <james.liu@orchidbank.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Increased 500s + latency from our reserved pool — urgent

Evelyn,

We're seeing a sustained surge of 500 responses and 2–3x tail latency from our dedicated pool starting ~07:58 PDT. This is hitting our transaction enrichment pipeline and causing timeouts upstream. Sample request IDs and a short log excerpt attached.

Key impact: 15% of inference calls are hitting 5xx, 30–40% increase in p95 latency. We are degrading checkout flows for high-value customers.

Can you confirm whether this is an internal scheduling/eviction issue or capacity saturation on your side? We need an immediate mitigation path and ETA for a fix.

- James Liu
VP of Engineering — OrchidBank
ops@orchidbank.com

Attachments: orchid-error-samples.log, request-ids-08-04.txt

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: James Liu <james.liu@orchidbank.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Increased 500s + latency from our reserved pool — urgent

Thanks James — filing and triaging now. Soojin/Marissa/Priyom, copying you for ops + eng. Quick ask: can infra confirm whether OrchidBank's reserved capacity is being saturated or if noisy-neighbor preemption is causing evictions from their pool? They report a p95 spike and a sustained 5xx wave.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: narrow down whether GPU OOMs / kernel failures / scheduler moves correspond to the request IDs in the log (attached).
- Priyom: snapshot reservation utilization and recent autoscale/burst events for their pool and any cross-tenant overlays in the last 30 minutes.
- Soojin: please acknowledge to James that we have this as Sev/P0 and give a short customer-facing note while we investigate.

I'll pull in AV/ops if we need temporary burst or cross-pool fallbacks. We should be prepared to request emergency burst capacity if this looks like a saturation event.

— Evelyn

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: James Liu <james.liu@orchidbank.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Increased 500s + latency from our reserved pool — urgent

Update from infra triage (summary):
- Observed behavior: Orchids' dedicated pool (pool-id: dp-00721) hit sustained token-queue depth that exceeded configured headroom at ~07:52 PDT, coincident with a high-cost batch from another tenant (noisy neighbor) that consumed spare slots on the same GPU shard. Several worker processes reported transient kernel fallback to CPU for long sequences, producing multi-second tail latencies and occasional 5xx when KV cache sync timed out.
- Evidence: Correlated request IDs in the attached log show kernel fallback traces and evictions; scheduler logs show concurrent burst by tenant t-9142 beginning 07:50. No persistent OOMs were found on Orchid's pinned workers.

Actionable mitigation (short term, ETA 30–45 minutes):
1) Emergency burst authorization: request temporary +25% burst capacity on OrchidBank's dedicated pool to drain queue and restore p95. Requires exec/finance sign-off for burst billing.
2) Fast routing fallback: route new requests for Orchid to a compatible, lower-cost model variant on an underutilized shard (approx +100–200ms but will drop 5xx). Requires config toggle from runtime (we can flip in ~10 minutes).
3) Noisy-neighbor throttle: place a soft throttle on tenant t-9142 for 60 minutes; this reduces cross-tenant contention while we validate longer-term isolation.

Longer-term: add stricter shard isolation and revise autoscale burst policy to cap single-tenant spikes. Recommend a postmortem and a credit/contract concession discussion with the account team.

Customer-facing ask: if exec approves emergency burst, we will: authorize burst, run routing fallback for ~20–30 minutes while queue drains, then roll back fallback. Otherwise we can flip routing fallback immediately but will need to accept small latency increase for some endpoints.

Attachments: triage-scheduler-snippets.txt (uploaded to Jira INF-1432), Orch-request-ids-correlated.csv (referenced in Jira).

Requesting: Evelyn — please coordinate a short exec approval for one-time burst (+25%) and confirm whether Finance is ok with emergency billing terms; Soojin — please share the customer note below if you want to use the immediate routing fallback without burst.

— Marissa
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference
